item.title: Oyaki: Nagano's Savoury Stuffed Dumplings — Guide
item.description: Oyaki are one of Nagano’s most beloved home-style foods, round dumplings of wheat or buckwheat dough wrapped around a savoury (or sometimes sweet) filling, then grilled, steamed or baked, historically a practical staple in a mountainous region where rice was harder to grow. Common fillings include nozawana pickled greens, eggplant, sweet red bean and seasonal vegetables, and the dumplings are sold at specialty shops, markets and roadside stands throughout the prefecture as a warm, satisfying and affordable local snack.

item.title: Shinshu Soba & Nagano Food Guide: What to Eat in the Japan Alps
item.description: Nagano Prefecture has one of the most distinctive regional food traditions in Japan — shaped by a landlocked mountain climate, heavy snowfall, intense cold, and the need to preserve food through long winters. The absence of a coastline drove the development of an extraordinary preserved-food culture: lacto-fermented vegetables (tsukemono), long-aged miso from locally grown soybean and barley, smoke-dried mountain trout and carp, dried mushrooms and wild vegetables gathered from the alpine forests.
